text:
Jimmy Snuggerud is scoring like a sniper in his second NHL season: nine goals in 17 games, six in his last ten, and a power-play goal in Nashville on Saturday. He's 22, the 23rd pick in 2022, and the Blues are giving him nearly 18 minutes a night.

The honest version: the chances are good, the finishing is hotter than that. He has nine goals on 4.6 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 23% against 12% last season, and St. Louis has scored 5.9 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Both numbers usually drift back.

What makes us think the player is real is where he shoots from. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.7 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 96th percentile among forwards, and 29% of his setups came from behind the net, a strange and useful habit. Evolving-Hockey's worry is defense: opponents created more with him out there. Our projection sees about 32 goals, which would still be a big step up from 21 last season.
